item.title: Urgent Safety Concern – Dangerous Build-Up of Leaves on Kings Hall Road and Reddons Road, 25th November
item.description:
I would like to raise an urgent concern regarding the significant build-up of fallen leaves along Kings Hall Road and onto Reddons Road. This issue was originally reported two weeks ago, but unfortunately, no action has been taken. The leaves are now becoming extremely deep, creating a serious safety hazard for pedestrians. Please could arrangements be made to clear the leaves by hand rather than using a machine, as soon as possible? Given that this was reported two weeks ago and the situation is becoming increasingly dangerous, I would appreciate your urgent attention to this matter before someone has an accident. Thank you for your assistance, and I look forward to your prompt response.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Kings Hall Road, Penge, Greater London

item.title: 34 Dartmouth Park Hill, 25th November
item.description:
I am writing to report a pedestrian safety and accessibility obstruction on the pavement at the junction of Wyndham Crescent and Dartmouth Park Hill, directly adjacent to Nos. 32A and 34 Dartmouth Park Hill. Overgrown bushes and trees encroaching from the boundary along this stretch have severely narrowed the usable width of the footway. In several places, it is impossible for two pedestrians to pass each other safely on the pavement—forcing one person to stop and give way, step into neighbouring front gardens to clear the path, or risk stepping toward the carriageway. Combined with the current road works and temporary traffic controls at the junction, this also creates a blind spot when turning into or out of Wyndham Crescent. Please could the Highways / Street Environment team inspect this section of footway and arrange for the overhanging vegetation to be cut back so the full width of the pavement and junction sightlines are restored? I have attached a recent photograph showing the extent of the encroachment and the narrowing at the corner.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Dartmouth Park Hill, Archway, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
